title: Coordinate representing family before published support transport
statement: Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a compactification of a $k$-morphism $X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $R_W$ be the actual coefficient reduction/total-limit calculus, let $M$ be an integral compact-support model, and let $S,G,H,D,h_D$ be the strict etale compact-support, Brown, finite-evaluation and transported comparison data. Use the interfaces of [def-pur-integral-representing-pair-data]. Then the coordinate family exists: for every integral input $L$ and supplied exceptional system $A$, it gives a Pair whose Hom equivalence uses coordinate support, its actual counit and theta. These pairs obey the Family naturality formulas, including actual-system squares detected from level squares only for systems concentrated in a common degree. This conclusion does not yet transport Hom maps or trace equations to the published compact-support functor and its alpha.

proof.text: Put $C=\mathcal R_YL$ and $B_K=\mathcal R_XK$. By [lem-pur-integral-reduction-uniform-tor], these reductions have uniformly bounded finite-Tor constructible evaluations and compatible etale-origin witnesses. They are normalized by [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps]. Exact evaluation detects a common lower bound in the system category: $e_nH^q(B_K)=H^q((B_K)_n)$, so vanishing at all levels means the strict cohomology system is zero [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. The same applies to $C$. The supplied $\phi_n$ and common interval for $M_n$ give the common lower bound for $Rf_n^!L_n$. Consequently [lem-pur-brown-tower-finite-site-comparison] applies to $C$: $N$ is bounded below and normalized, with counit-preserving identifications $c_n:N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$ and precisely the stated exceptional quotient transitions. It supplies the actual system counit $\epsilon:FN\to C$ and the natural $R$-linear Brown bijection for every $B_K$.

proof.text: In case (a), use the supplied $\theta$. In case (b), set $\psi_n=c_n^{-1}\phi_n:M_n\to N_n$. Since evaluations are exact and cohomology of strict systems is componentwise, $M_\bullet$ and $N$ have cohomology only in degree $r$ [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison, lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence]. Apply [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] to their shifts by $r$ in the abelian category of systems, and also to each evaluation. It gives functorial identifications $\delta_V:V\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r(V)[-r]$, commuting with evaluations. Compatibility of $\psi_n$ with transition adjoints gives compatibility with the underlying semilinear transitions by the defining tensor/restriction adjunction. Applying $H^r$, the maps $H^r(\psi_n)$ therefore constitute a strict system isomorphism $a:H^r(M_\bullet)\to H^r(N)$; its inverses also commute with transitions, by multiplying the same squares by the inverses. Define $\theta=\delta_N^{-1}\circ a[-r]\circ\delta_{M_\bullet}$. The naturality and Hom bijection in the truncation lemma imply $e_n\theta=\psi_n$, not merely equality on cohomology. For two data sets in the same degree, conjugate either proposed compatibility square by the $\delta$ maps. Its sides are maps of strict cohomology systems and are equal exactly when their component maps are equal. Hence level-identification squares give the required actual system square.

proof.text: The integral category uses intrinsic completeness. Apply [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence] to identify this with derived completeness and with invertibility of the specified quotient augmentation. Thus [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] gives invertible actual units $u_L$, $u_K$, $u_{P_RK}$ and the actual system counit $e_{M_\bullet}:\mathcal R_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}M_\bullet$. Here $P_RK$ is in the integral category by [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. The unit and counit are those of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], not arbitrarily chosen reconstruction isomorphisms. For integral $A,D$ the map $q\mapsto\mathcal R_T(q)$ on Hom sets is bijective: it is the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal R_TA,\mathcal R_TD)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_TD)$ followed by composition with $u_D^{-1}$. Its inverse on a system map $z$ is $u_D^{-1}\mathcal L_T(z)u_A$, by the unit naturality and triangle identities. This uses full Hom sets in the ambient derived categories, as required by the full integral subcategories.

proof.text:
Compose the following bijections, writing $M=\mathcal L_XM_\bullet$:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathsf S_X)}(B_K,M_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\theta\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathsf S_X)}(B_K,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathsf S_Y)}(FB_K,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P_RK,L).$$
The first is the actual reduction/limit adjunction [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; the middle one is [lem-pur-brown-tower-finite-site-comparison], with its bounded-below etale-origin domain checked in Step 1; the last uses the coordinate counit $\alpha_K$ and Step 3. Explicitly, $h:K\to M$ gives
$$v_h=\theta\,e_{M_\bullet}\,\mathcal R_X(h),\quad w_h=\epsilon\,F(v_h),\quad \Phi_K(h)=u_L^{-1}\mathcal L_Y(w_h\alpha_K)u_{P_RK}.$$
Each bijection is natural in $K$. The Brown bijection is $R$-linear by its cited statement. The outer adjunction bijections are $R$-linear because their formulas compose the unit/counit with the $R$-linear reduction and total-limit functors: those are derived tensor and derived limit of $R$-module sheaves. Composition with $\theta$ and $\alpha_K$ is also $R$-linear. Hence their composite has all the claimed linearity and naturality.

proof.text: For $h=1_M$, the preceding formula has $v_h=\theta e_{M_\bullet}$ and $w_h=\epsilon F(\theta)F(e_{M_\bullet})$. Set $z=w_h\alpha_M:\mathcal R_YP_RM\to\mathcal R_YL$ and $t=u_L^{-1}\mathcal L_Y(z)u_{P_RM}$. Then $\mathcal R_Y(t)=z$ as an actual system map. Indeed naturality gives $e_{\mathcal R_YL}\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y(z)=z e_{\mathcal R_YP_RM}$, while the triangle identities give $e_{\mathcal R_YP_RM}\mathcal R_Y(u_{P_RM})=1$ and $e_{\mathcal R_YL}=(\mathcal R_Yu_L)^{-1}$. Substitution proves the equality, using [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and the invertible units of Step 3. Therefore $\mathcal R_Y(t)\alpha_M^{-1}=\epsilon F(\theta)F(e_{M_\bullet})$, exactly the claimed ordinary-system formula. Naturality in $K$ also shows $\Phi_K(h)=t\circ P_R(h)$ by applying it to $h:K\to M$ and $1_M$; thus $(M,t)$ is the asserted representing pair.

proof.text: Evaluate the actual equality in Step 5 at $n$. The counit-preserving comparisons of [lem-pur-brown-tower-finite-site-comparison] identify $e_n\epsilon$ with $\epsilon_n$ and $e_n\theta$ with $\phi_n$ after the comparison $c_n$. The evaluations of $\alpha_M$ are the specified compact-support comparisons [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. The evaluation of $e_{M_\bullet}$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of the total-limit projection [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], which is precisely the canonical reduction identification in the hypotheses. Under these identifications the evaluated composite is $t_n=\epsilon_n\circ F_n(\phi_n)$. This deduction evaluates an equality already proved in the derived category of systems; it does not infer equality of arbitrary system morphisms from their evaluations.

proof.text: For two supplied data sets, write $b:L\to L'$ and $a:M_\bullet\to M'_\bullet$ for the given maps, with $\theta'a=G(\mathcal R_Yb)\theta$, and put $m=\mathcal L_X(a)$. Naturality of the reduction/limit counit gives $a e_{M_\bullet}=e_{M'_\bullet}\mathcal R_X(m)$. Consequently, for $h:K\to M$, $v'_{mh}=G(\mathcal R_Yb)v_h$. Naturality of the Brown counit implies $\epsilon'F(v'_{mh})=(\mathcal R_Yb)\epsilon F(v_h)$ [lem-pur-brown-tower-finite-site-comparison]. Using the natural units and $\alpha$ in the formula of Step 4 now gives $\Phi'_K(mh)=b\Phi_K(h)$. With $K=M,h=1_M$ and naturality in $K$, this reads $t'P_R(m)=bt$. This proves both naturality assertions. In case (b) Step 2 supplies the needed system square from the stated level squares for a common degree $r$. All constructions concern only the supplied input and the Brown Hom bijections on their verified domains.
